title: Population Distribution and Left-Right Voting
text:
This study aims to investigate the effects of different historical developments of ideological spectrum (left/right) on the relationship between urban-rural population distribution and the general election voting.
There are noted findings in the political science literature that rural areas tend to vote for right wing parties while more urban areas for left. However, different countries present different political histories, and in particular, the development of the breadth of left-right spectrum and the voters’ loyalty to their ideologies over time.
In this project, I compare the presidential elections of France-2022 and the USA-2020. I analyze how different the relationship between urban-rural population distribution and left-right voting behavior in France and in the USA.
I hypothesize that two reasons will effect differences in this relationship: first is the stronger tradition of left-wing politics in France; and the second is the wider spectrum of left-wing ideologies. The longer history of leftism can create a closer political affiliation between the rural population and the left-wing parties. The wider spectrum of political ideologies, on the other hand, can present various opportunities for political parties to establish rapport with the rural populations. This is because in a wider political spectrum, not only the number of parties are higher, but also the substantial issue positions adopted by parties can offer a higher variety in their combinations. In a biparty system, issue positions, such as A, B, C, D, are divided into two, while in a multiparty system the issue positions are not only divided into more sections, but also they are adopted by parties with overlaps such as Party-X can adopt A and B while Party-Y can adopt B and D. Since France has a multi-party system, multiple parties can address the interests of the rural voters in different ways, preventing the concentration of vote.

French 2022 Presidential Election Results (R1) Tabular vote counts for each candidate at the commune level. Converted into Left/Right blocs.
https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/election-presidentielle-des-10-et-24-avril-2022-resultats-definitifs-du-1er-tour/
French Population Distribution INSEE UU2020 (Unités Urbaines) Tabular classification of communes as Urban vs Rural. Joined by INSEE commune code.
https://www.insee.fr/fr/information/4802589
French Geometry Data IGN Admin Express (Commune Polygons – for merging) Official French administrative boundaries. Polygon spatial data at the commune level (higher resolution than US counties). Used for all France maps. This file is large and is not auto-downloaded; it must be obtained separately.
2020 Presidential Election Results (MIT Election Lab) Tabular vote counts at the county level. Joined to polygons using GEOID identifiers. Allows derivation of Left vs Right vote shares.
https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi%3A10.7910%2FDVN%2FVOQCHQ￼
American urban-rural population (RUCC 2023) Rural–Urban Continuum Codes from USDA ERS. Tabular (non-spatial) data describing each county’s classification. Joined to county geometries using the county GEOID.
https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/rural-urban-continuum-codes
County Geometries (TIGER/Line 2023) Provided by the U.S. Census Bureau. Polygon spatial data, each polygon representing a full county boundary. Accessed directly via the {tigris} package.

title: Population Distribution and Left-Right Voting
text:
Maps


Show code
# -----------------------------
# 1) Commune geometries from france_geosp.gpkg
# -----------------------------
gpkg_path


[1] "data/france_geosp.gpkg"


Show code
# We explicitly choose the polygon commune layer:
fr_communes <- sf::st_read(gpkg_path, layer = "commune", quiet = TRUE) |>
  janitor::clean_names()

# Find an INSEE commune code column and standardize to 'code_insee'
insee_candidates <- c(
  "code_insee",
  "code_insee_de_la_commune",  # present in some Admin Express builds
  "insee_com",
  "codgeo",
  "insee_cod",
  "insee_code",
  "com"
)

have_insee <- intersect(names(fr_communes), insee_candidates)
if (length(have_insee) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find an INSEE commune code column in france_geosp.gpkg (commune layer). ",
       "Available columns: ", paste(names(fr_communes), collapse = ", "))
}

fr_communes <- fr_communes |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    code_insee = sprintf("%05s", as.character(.data[[have_insee[1]]]))
  )

# ---- Filter to mainland France (approximate lon/lat box) ----
centroids <- sf::st_centroid(fr_communes)

fr_communes <- fr_communes |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    lon = sf::st_coordinates(centroids)[, 1],
    lat = sf::st_coordinates(centroids)[, 2]
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    lon > -6, lon < 10,
    lat > 41, lat < 52
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-lon, -lat)

# -----------------------------
# 2) INSEE Unités urbaines 2020 (urban / rural)
# -----------------------------
uu_zip <- "data/france_UU2020_commune.zip"
uu_dir <- "data/uu2020"
if (!dir.exists(uu_dir)) dir.create(uu_dir)

# Unzip if needed
unzip(uu_zip, exdir = uu_dir)

uu_file <- list.files(
  uu_dir,
  pattern = "UU2020.*[.](xlsx|csv|CSV|XLSX)$",
  full.names = TRUE
)[1]

if (is.na(uu_file)) {
  stop("Could not find a UU2020 .xlsx or .csv file inside ", uu_dir,
       ". Please open the zip manually once and check the filenames.")
}

if (grepl("\\.xlsx$", uu_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
  uu_raw <- readxl::read_xlsx(
    uu_file,
    sheet = "Composition_communale",
    skip  = 5
  )
} else {
  uu_raw <- readr::read_csv2(
    uu_file,
    locale    = readr::locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
    guess_max = 50000
  )
}

uu <- uu_raw |>
  janitor::clean_names()

nm <- names(uu)

uu_code_col <- nm[grepl("codgeo|code_commune|code_insee", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)]
uu_urban_col <- nm[grepl("uu2020|unite_urbaine|code_uu", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)]

if (length(uu_code_col) == 0 || length(uu_urban_col) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Could not find commune code (e.g. codgeo) or UU code (e.g. uu2020) in UU2020 file.\n",
    "Columns are: ", paste(nm, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

uu_communes <- uu |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    code_insee = sprintf("%05s", as.character(.data[[uu_code_col[1]]])),
    urban_rural_fr = dplyr::case_when(
      type_commune_uu == "Unité urbaine"      ~ "Urban",
      type_commune_uu == "Hors unité urbaine" ~ "Rural",
      TRUE                                    ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(code_insee, urban_rural_fr)

# -----------------------------
# 3) French 2022 R1 election results (commune-level, WIDE format)
# -----------------------------
elex_path_csv <- fr_elex_path

if (!file.exists(elex_path_csv)) {
  stop(
    "Could not find the French election CSV at '", elex_path_csv, "'.\n",
    "Make sure the file is there. Current working directory is: ", getwd()
  )
}

header_line <- readLines(elex_path_csv, n = 1, encoding = "UTF-8")

comma_n <- stringr::str_count(header_line, ",")
semi_n  <- stringr::str_count(header_line, ";")

delim_guess <- if (semi_n > comma_n) ";" else ","

elex_raw <- readr::read_delim(
  elex_path_csv,
  delim = delim_guess,
  locale = readr::locale(encoding = "UTF-8"),
  guess_max = 200000,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

elex <- elex_raw |>
  janitor::clean_names()

nm_elex <- names(elex)

code_col <- nm_elex[grepl("code_insee", nm_elex, ignore.case = TRUE)]

if (length(code_col) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Columns are: ", paste(nm_elex, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Left/Right candidate lists (binary bloc classification)
left_tokens <- c("MÉLENCHON", "MELENCHON",
                 "JADOT",
                 "ROUSSEL",
                 "HIDALGO",
                 "POUTOU",
                 "ARTHAUD")

right_tokens <- c("MACRON",
                  "LE PEN", "LEPEN",
                  "ZEMMOUR",
                  "PÉCRESSE", "PECRESSE",
                  "DUPONT-AIGNAN", "DUPONT AIGNAN",
                  "LASSALLE")

# Identify candidate name and vote columns (nom_*, voix_*)
nom_cols  <- grep("^nom",  nm_elex, value = TRUE)
voix_cols <- grep("^voix", nm_elex, value = TRUE)

if (length(nom_cols) == 0 || length(voix_cols) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Could not find any 'nom*' or 'voix*' columns in the election data.\n",
    "Columns are: ", paste(nm_elex, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

nom_idx  <- match(nom_cols,  nm_elex)
voix_idx <- match(voix_cols, nm_elex)

nom_cols  <- nom_cols[order(nom_idx)]
voix_cols <- voix_cols[order(voix_idx)]

if (length(nom_cols) != length(voix_cols)) {
  stop(
    "Different number of 'nom*' and 'voix*' columns. Cannot reliably pair candidates.\n",
    "nom_cols: ", paste(nom_cols, collapse = ", "),
    "\nvoix_cols: ", paste(voix_cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

cand_meta <- data.frame(
  nom_col  = nom_cols,
  voix_col = voix_cols,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cand_meta$candidate <- vapply(
  cand_meta$nom_col,
  function(col) {
    vals <- as.character(elex[[col]])
    vals[which(!is.na(vals))[1]]
  },
  character(1)
)

cand_meta$bloc_lr <- dplyr::case_when(
  cand_meta$candidate %in% left_tokens  ~ "Left",
  cand_meta$candidate %in% right_tokens ~ "Right",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

dept_col <- nm_elex[grepl("code_du_departement", nm_elex, ignore.case = TRUE)][1]

elex <- elex |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(cand_meta$voix_col),
      ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dept = stringr::str_pad(
      as.character(.data[[dept_col]]),
      width = 2,
      side  = "left",
      pad   = "0"
    ),
    com  = stringr::str_pad(
      as.character(.data[[code_col[1]]]),
      width = 3,
      side  = "left",
      pad   = "0"
    ),
    code_insee = paste0(dept, com)
  )

left_voix_cols  <- cand_meta$voix_col[cand_meta$bloc_lr == "Left"]
right_voix_cols <- cand_meta$voix_col[cand_meta$bloc_lr == "Right"]

if (length(left_voix_cols) == 0 || length(right_voix_cols) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No left and/or right candidates detected in cand_meta.\n",
    "cand_meta:\n",
    paste(utils::capture.output(print(cand_meta)), collapse = "\n")
  )
}

elex_lr <- elex |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    left_votes = rowSums(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(left_voix_cols)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    right_votes = rowSums(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(right_voix_cols)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(code_insee) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    left_votes  = sum(left_votes,  na.rm = TRUE),
    right_votes = sum(right_votes, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_lr    = left_votes + right_votes,
    left_share  = dplyr::if_else(total_lr > 0, left_votes / total_lr, NA_real_),
    right_share = dplyr::if_else(total_lr > 0, right_votes / total_lr, NA_real_),
    lr_margin   = left_share - right_share,
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

# -----------------------------
# 5) Join geometry + UU (urban/rural) + voting
# -----------------------------
fr_map <- fr_communes |>
  dplyr::left_join(uu_communes, by = "code_insee") |>
  dplyr::left_join(elex_lr,   by = "code_insee")

# -----------------------------
# 6) Map 1 — Urban vs Rural communes
# -----------------------------
p_fr_urban <- ggplot2::ggplot(fr_map) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = urban_rural_fr),
    color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values   = c("Urban" = "#7b3294", "Rural" = "#e66101"),
    na.value = "grey90",
    drop     = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "France — Communes classified as Urban vs Rural (INSEE UU2020)",
    subtitle = "Purple = Urban (commune en unité urbaine), \n Orange = Rural (hors unité urbaine)",
    fill     = "Urban–Rural",
    caption  = "Data: IGN Admin Express (communes, polygons), INSEE UU2020"
  )

#                                   p_fr_urban

# -----------------------------
# 7) Map 2 — Left vs Right leading bloc by commune
# -----------------------------
fr_map <- fr_map |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    lr_winner = dplyr::case_when(
      lr_margin > 0  ~ "Left",
      lr_margin < 0  ~ "Right",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

p_fr_lr <- ggplot2::ggplot(fr_map) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = lr_winner),
    color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values   = c("Left" = "#08519c", "Right" = "#cb181d"),
    na.value = "grey90",
    drop     = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "France — Left vs Right Leading Bloc by Commune\nPrésidentielle 2022, 1er tour",
    subtitle = "Blue = Left-bloc lead, Red = Right-bloc lead",
    fill     = "Leading bloc",
    caption  = "Data: Ministère de l’Intérieur (2022 R1),\n IGN Admin Express (communes, polygons), INSEE UU2020"
  )

#                                   p_fr_lr

# -----------------------------
# 8) Map 3 — Urban communes & Left-leaning Urban communes
# -----------------------------
fr_map <- fr_map |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    lr_winner = dplyr::case_when(
      lr_margin > 0  ~ "Left",
      lr_margin < 0  ~ "Right",
      TRUE           ~ NA_character_
    ),
    is_left_urban = (urban_rural_fr == "Urban" & lr_winner == "Left"),
    cat3 = dplyr::case_when(
      is_left_urban             ~ "Left & Urban",
      urban_rural_fr == "Urban" ~ "Urban only",
      TRUE                      ~ "Other"
    )
  )

p_fr_left_urban <- ggplot2::ggplot(fr_map) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = cat3),
    color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Other"        = "grey90",
      "Urban only"   = "#9e9ac8",
      "Left & Urban" = "#542788"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "France — Urban Communes and Left-Leaning Urban Communes",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Light purple: all Urban communes (INSEE UU2020)",
      "Dark purple: communes that are BOTH Urban\n and Left-leaning in 2022 (1st round)",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    fill     = NULL,
    caption  = "Data: Ministère de l’Intérieur (2022 R1), \n IGN Admin Express (communes, polygons), INSEE UU2020"
  )

#                             p_fr_left_urban

# -----------------------------
# 9) Map 4 — Rural communes and Right-leaning Rural communes
# -----------------------------
fr_map <- fr_map |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    lr_winner = dplyr::case_when(
      lr_margin > 0  ~ "Left",
      lr_margin < 0  ~ "Right",
      TRUE           ~ NA_character_
    ),
    is_right_rural = (urban_rural_fr == "Rural" & lr_winner == "Right"),
    cat4 = dplyr::case_when(
      is_right_rural             ~ "Right & Rural",
      urban_rural_fr == "Rural"  ~ "Rural only",
      TRUE                       ~ "Other"
    )
  )

p_fr_right_rural <- ggplot2::ggplot(fr_map) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = cat4),
    color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Other"         = "grey90",
      "Rural only"    = "#FADADD",
      "Right & Rural" = "#8B0000"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "France — Rural Communes and Right-Leaning Rural Communes",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Light orange: all Rural communes (INSEE UU2020)",
      "Dark orange: communes that are BOTH Rural and\n Right-leaning in 2022 (1st round)",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    fill     = NULL,
    caption  = "Data: Ministère de l’Intérieur (2022 R1), \n IGN Admin Express (communes, polygons), INSEE UU2020"
  )

#                               p_fr_right_rural
